name: iris_brainstem
title: Iris Brainstem - power, USB and servo hub (B2) for the Iris robot head
brief: Iris Brainstem is board B2 of Iris, a human-eyed robot head (Iris design spec v0.1, section 4.2). It sits flat in the head's base (64 x 80 mm, 4 layers, F face up at H Z -60). A USB-C PD sink (CH224K, CFG pins hard-tied for 9 V) feeds a 5 A fuse and a 10 mOhm shunt read by an INA226 (0x40); a TPS565208 makes 6V0_SERVO (5 A, off until SERVO_EN) for ten 5264-type servo ports in two banks of five (J10-J19, D V G, servo IDs per spec 5), and a TPS56339 makes 5V2, diode-ORed with a second, data-only USB-C's VBUS into 5V_SYS for B1 Cortex. The SCS bus driver is the Feetech / Waveshare auto-direction circuit (74LVC1G126 + 74LVC1G125 + MMBT3906) on 3V3_B2 from an AP2112K. A MAX98357A drives a speaker on a JST SH-2. Two JST SH harness headers (H1 SH-10, H2 SH-7) carry power, USB, the bus, I2C and I2S to B1 exactly as spec 5 binds them.

blocks.title: M2 holes on the base plate bosses
USB-C PD 9 V input: CH224K, TVS, 5 A fuse, 10 mOhm shunt

netClasses.name: PDIN
netClasses.why: the 9 V input path, J1 VBUS through F1 and R1 to both buck inputs (spec 6: 0.68 A typical, about 4.3 A for milliseconds). 0.6 mm is the width of the receptacle's VBUS pads and of the TPS565208 / TPS56339 VIN pins (pd_brick: nothing wider enters between the HRO's GND and SBU pads). The tracks only connect the path; board.zones carry the current (see README)

netClasses.name: SERVO
netClasses.why: the servo rail from L1 to the 2 x 470 uF and the ten 5264 ports (burst 4.6 A, buck limit 5 A). 0.8 mm still enters the 0603 feedback resistor's pad; In2 is poured 6V0_SERVO and board.zones lay the bank strips after routing

netClasses.name: SWNODE
netClasses.why: the two switch nodes: 0.6 mm is the SOT-23-6 SW pin; each node is a few millimetres from pin to inductor, widened by an F.Cu zone after routing

netClasses.name: RAIL5V
netClasses.why: 5V2 and 5V_SYS (5V_SYS peak 1.56 A est., spec 6): 0.6 mm, about 1.65 A at a 10 C rise on 1 oz outer copper. A 0.8 mm class was tried (2026-10-03): Freerouting then ran both rails the long way on In2 (0.5 oz), which rates lower, so the class stays 0.6 mm and board.zones widen the routed path

netClasses.name: USBVBUS
netClasses.why: the data port's VBUS to its Schottky: 0.6 mm is the receptacle's VBUS pad width (nothing wider enters between its GND and SBU pads, pd_brick); USB 2.0 ports give 0.5 A, about 1.6 A at a 10 C rise

shape.why: spec 4.2 / fig/board_briefs.json B2: 64.0 x 80.0 mm, fillet 3.0 (binding outline)

rules.why_rules: 0.15 mm clearance and 0.2 mm default track inside JLC's multilayer window (0.09 mm); 0.6 / 0.3 mm vias

keepouts.why: M2 screw head on top and the base-plate boss below (H (X -34, Y +28))

keepouts.name: boss_h2

keepouts.why: M2 screw head on top and the base-plate boss below (H (X -106, Y -28))

keepouts.name: bcu_bank_left
keepouts.why: B.Cu under the left servo bank and the 6V0 node (L1, its output caps, C1) is the 6V0_SERVO zone: a signal track there would cut it into islands

keepouts.name: bcu_front_bar
keepouts.why: the 6V0_SERVO bar on B.Cu along the front edge that joins the two bank strips (it runs below the bosses' keep-outs)

keepouts.name: bcu_bank_right
keepouts.why: B.Cu under the right servo bank: 6V0 zone

keepouts.name: bcu_spine
keepouts.why: the 5V_SYS spine on B.Cu from the diode-OR to H1

keepouts.name: bcu_spine_rear
keepouts.why: the 5V_SYS spine's rear arm under D2, C20 and D3

keepouts.name: bcu_vin
keepouts.why: the VIN corridor on B.Cu from the shunt to both buck inputs (and the left bank's rear ports' 6V0)

keepouts.name: bcu_input
keepouts.why: B.Cu under the input column (J1 VBUS, F1, R1): VBUS_PD zone

keepouts.name: in2_input
keepouts.why: keeps In2 signal tracks out of the input column so the VBUS_PD and VIN zones find via sites (a stitch via must clear other nets' tracks on every layer)

keepouts.name: in2_buck6
keepouts.why: the servo buck's input via fields (VIN beside the caps' VIN pads, GND beside their GND pads)

keepouts.name: in2_out6
keepouts.why: the servo buck's output via fields (GND left of the output caps, 6V0 between them and L1)

keepouts.name: in2_buck5
keepouts.why: the 5V2 buck's VIN via field; kept off its GND side, where the USB pair needs In2 to leave the rear right (with it there the USB D- line stayed open, 2026-10-03)

zones.name: vbus_pd
zones.why: J1's two VBUS pads, the TVS cathode and F1's input pad on both outer layers; it touches the receptacle's VBUS pads from above

zones.name: vin_f
zones.why: F1's output pad to the shunt's fuse-side pad (1.4 mm apart) and the INA226 IN+ filter resistor, on F.Cu: a B.Cu copy found no via site and was an island

zones.name: vin_col
zones.why: the shunt's VIN pad, C3's + pad and the INA226 IN-/VBUS taps on both outer layers, stitched

zones.name: vin_band
zones.why: VIN on B.Cu from the input column to both buck inputs (signal tracks are kept off this band). Its priority is below vin_col, vin_u3 and vin_u4 so that their B.Cu fills, and with them their stitch vias, survive where they overlap it

zones.name: vin_u3
zones.why: U3's input caps' VIN pads (x 29.95) and the VIN pin, stitched down to the B.Cu band beside them

zones.name: vin_u4
zones.why: U4's input caps' VIN pads and the VIN pin, stitched down to the B.Cu band

zones.name: v6_b
zones.why: 6V0_SERVO on B.Cu as a U: a strip under each bank of five ports (with the node under L1 and C1 on the left) joined by a bar along the front edge, below the boss keep-outs

zones.name: v6_node
zones.why: L1's 6V0 pad, the output caps' 6V0 pads and C1's + pad on F.Cu, with a column of vias between the caps and L1 to the B.Cu strip and bar and to the In2 pour

zones.name: v6_bank_l
zones.why: the left bank's V pins (x 6.0) on F.Cu, between the DATA pins (x 3.5) and the G pins (x 8.5)

zones.name: v6_bank_r
zones.why: the right bank's V pins (x 58.0) on F.Cu, between its G pins (x 55.5) and DATA pins (x 60.5)

zones.name: v6_c2
zones.why: C2's + pad on F.Cu (the B.Cu under it is the 5V_SYS spine)

zones.name: gnd_out6
zones.why: the servo buck's output caps' GND pads joined solid and stitched to the In1 plane right beside them (the B.Cu under them is 6V0)

zones.name: gnd_in6
zones.why: the servo buck's input caps' GND pads (x 31.85) joined solid and stitched to In1 beside them

zones.name: gnd_in5
zones.why: the 5V2 buck's input caps' GND pads joined solid and stitched to In1

zones.name: gnd_front
zones.why: GND stitching along the front strip (headers, amplifier, bus driver), where B.Cu is ground: any board.zones GND zone stops the plan's own stitcher, so the zones stitch GND themselves

zones.name: gnd_mid
zones.why: GND stitching in the open middle (test-pad row), where B.Cu is ground

zones.name: gnd_rear
zones.why: GND stitching round the CH224K, the data port and the 5V_SYS parts, where B.Cu is ground

zones.name: v5_spine
zones.why: the 5V_SYS spine on B.Cu: a 5.4 mm column from the rear (D3, and D2 through an arm along y 61.2-63.4 that stays clear of U4's VIN via field) to just behind H1, where it turns under H1's 5V_SYS pins; signal tracks are kept off it

zones.name: v5_front
zones.why: H1's 5V_SYS pins (1 and 2) and C28 on F.Cu, down to the spine's front end

zones.name: v5_link_front
zones.why: vias from the spine's front end up to v5_front, on H1's side of the USB_DP track that runs down x 45.1 (a link right of it joined nothing, 2026-10-03)

zones.name: v5_link_rear
zones.why: D3's cathode on F.Cu stitched down to the spine

zones.name: v5_link_d2
zones.why: D2's cathode on F.Cu stitched down to the spine's rear arm

zones.name: sw_6v0
zones.why: fills the 0.8 mm gap between L1's pad 1 and U3's SW pin solid

zones.name: sw_5v2
zones.why: fills the gap between L2's pad 1 and U4's SW pin solid

zones.name: v5v2_out
zones.why: L2's output pad, the two 22 uF and D2's anode on F.Cu: the routed 0.6 mm track alone measured 0.51 mm at the min-cut (1.5 A at 10 C) against 5V_SYS's 1.56 A peak. The outline stays left of VIN's F.Cu track to U4 (x 33.5 and y 56.66) so no island forms beyond it

board.notes: Frame (spec 4.2, binding): F face up at H Z = -60.0; H Y = 32 - x, H X = -30 - y (mm from the outline's top-left corner). y = 0 is the front edge (toward the face), y = 80 the rear edge (back of the head). 4 layers: F.Cu / In1 GND plane / In2 routing, then a 6V0_SERVO pour / B.Cu, plus board.zones on the power path.
